rows.source: Publication attribution and edition
rows.usage: Supplied PDF cover and imprint, PDF pp. 1–2. Bibliographic comparison.
rows.finding: The supplied PDF front matter names Kenneth W. Allen and identifies China Aerospace Studies Institute as publisher. Edition or release date is recorded as November 15, 2021.
evidence: Overview of Females in the PLA Air Force (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Substantive argument and evidentiary scope
rows.usage: Supplied PDF pp. 4–5. Extracted argument in paraphrase.
rows.finding: Allen distinguishes officers, enlisted personnel, civilian cadre and civilian personnel, then uses pilot cohorts to illustrate changing access to career paths. The graduate total describes an accumulated training cohort, which has a different denominator from the number serving in a given year. This reading establishes the scope of the authors’ argument. Its interpretation and broader empirical inferences need case-specific primary evidence.
evidence: Overview of Females in the PLA Air Force (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Two-year service and the term yiwubing
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 6. Extracted claim in paraphrase. Allen applies the term yiwubing to compulsory-service personnel on the two-year term, including those who entered voluntarily.
rows.finding: Article 25 distinguishes compulsory servicemen from sergeants on voluntary service. Article 26 sets the compulsory term at two years. The law confirms the category and duration. The entry mechanism of a particular recruit needs an intake record.
evidence: 2021 Military Service Law as amended, promulgated August 20

rows.source: Authority to enroll women under military service law
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The statutory framework allows recruiting women according to service requirements. Related printed notes 33 on PDF p. 53.
rows.finding: Article 3 of the earlier conscription regulations explicitly allows collecting female citizens for active service as needed. Article 20 of the 2021 law carries forward that authority. These are statutory powers and do not establish how frequently compulsory recruitment occurred.
evidence: 2021 Military Service Law as amended, promulgated August 20

rows.source: Peking University quota compared with programme-wide policy
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The author reports separate female admissions ceilings at Peking University of 10 percent for undergraduates and 20 percent for graduates in 2015. Related printed notes 31 on PDF p. 53.
rows.finding: The CASI academy study distinguishes the national programme and its end, and the 2017 Hunan account confirms termination of new recruitment in that province. Neither source reproduces the 2015 Peking University intake rules. The university’s 2015 notice is needed to verify the two ceilings and any exception to the reported general limit.
evidence: GovInfo copy of the CASI academy study
Hunan government admissions report for the 2017 cycle

rows.source: Estimated female pilot-candidate attrition
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 19. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The author estimates around 50 percent attrition from about 700 recruits and over 360 graduates by late 2021. Related printed notes 56, 57 on PDF p. 54.
rows.finding: The two rounded counts imply about 49 percent non-graduation only if the numerator and denominator cover matched completed cohorts. The November 2018 dispatch records a future intake and shows why cohorts still in training must be reconciled. Neither source provides a complete recruit and graduate ledger or a matched male comparison.
evidence: CASI publisher summary of the female personnel study (GovInfo PDF)
Xinhua’s November 2018 interview on 2019 pilot intake

rows.source: 2019 female student-pilot intake target
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 23. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper describes a 40-person 2019 female cadet cohort. Related printed notes 88 on PDF p. 55.
rows.finding: Xinhua’s November 2018 dispatch quoting the Air Force recruitment official verifies the 2019 target of 40. Its future tense leaves the number who matriculated or graduated open. A 2019 intake list would settle the difference.
evidence: Xinhua’s November 2018 interview on 2019 pilot intake

rows.source: First crewed Shenzhou flight date
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. Shenzhou 5 successfully flew with a crew in October 2003. Related printed notes 101 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The programme’s mission archive identifies Yang Liwei and the October 15–16 flight. This establishes the baseline used in the report’s astronaut chronology.
evidence: China Manned Space Engineering agency record of the first crewed flight

rows.source: Women entered the second astronaut group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The second group included China’s first two women selected for its astronaut programme. Related printed notes 103 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: Yang Liwei’s 2014 news conference gives the second selection and April 2010 induction, naming Liu Yang and Wang Yaping among the seven recruits. This confirms the intake result. The agency release does not give the candidate denominator.
evidence: Yang Liwei on the second astronaut selection, official September 2014 news conference

rows.source: Candidate denominators for the second astronaut group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The author reports two women selected from 15 candidates and five men selected from 30. Related printed notes 103 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The news conference supports five men and two women in the seven successful candidates. It records neither denominator. The September 2009 candidate reporting and the screening-stage lists must be reconciled before calculating sex-specific selection rates.
evidence: Yang Liwei on the second astronaut selection, official September 2014 news conference

rows.source: Liu Yang’s June 2012 flight
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. Liu Yang became the first Chinese woman to fly in space on Shenzhou 9. Related printed notes 104 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The mission agency’s dated post-flight release identifies her on the crew and records the national first. It reports the June 29 return after the mission. The separate pilot school history should be sourced on its own.
evidence: Shenzhou 9 programme archive, post-flight crew and mission account

rows.source: Wang Yaping’s birth year
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper gives 1978 or 1980 as possible birth years for Wang Yaping. Related printed notes 106 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The programme agency biography gives January 1980. Treat 1980 as the agency’s recorded year and retain 1978 only as an earlier conflicting attribution.
evidence: China Manned Space Engineering, Wang Yaping biography

rows.source: Wang Yaping’s Shenzhou 10 assignment
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. Wang Yaping flew on Shenzhou 10 in June 2013. Related printed notes 106 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The astronaut’s official profile gives June 11–26, 2013 for the flight. This independently confirms her assignment and the year.
evidence: China Manned Space Engineering, Wang Yaping biography

rows.source: Wang Yaping’s first spacewalk moved from forecast to recorded event
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The 2021 report expected Wang to become the first Chinese woman to undertake a spacewalk. Related printed notes 107 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The programme office records her departure from the station airlock on the evening of November 7, 2021, Beijing time, and identifies her as the first Chinese woman to perform a spacewalk. This is a documented result as distinct from the forecast in note 107.
evidence: China Manned Space Engineering, first Shenzhou 13 spacewalk dispatch

rows.source: Third astronaut-group selection announcement date
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. An 18-person third group had been selected by March 2021. Related printed notes 108 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The agency announced the completed 18-person selection on October 1, 2020. Yang Liwei’s March 2021 interview confirms that the selected group was already in place. March is a progress report date and should not be cited as the original selection date.
evidence: China Manned Space Engineering Office’s October 2020 selection release

rows.source: Role breakdown in the third astronaut group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The 18 selected astronaut candidates included seven pilots, seven flight engineers and four payload experts. Related printed notes 108 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The programme office publishes all three subtotals, which sum to 18. It describes these as selection categories. Later mission participation is a separate count.
evidence: China Manned Space Engineering Office’s October 2020 selection release

rows.source: Third astronaut-group applicant pool
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The group was selected from about 2,500 candidates after a process begun in May 2018. Related printed notes 108 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The selection notice gives May 2018, approximately 2,500 candidates and three stages. The initial pool is approximate and should not be used as an exact denominator.
evidence: China Manned Space Engineering Office’s October 2020 selection release

rows.source: Third group widened the eligible occupational backgrounds
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The third intake expanded selection beyond serving Air Force pilots. Related printed notes 108 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The office says pilots came from the active Air Force, engineers from aerospace and related disciplines, and payload experts from research personnel. This supports the scope change without establishing that entrants’ general fitness standards were lower.
evidence: China Manned Space Engineering Office’s October 2020 selection release

rows.source: Female intake into dual-registration university training
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 23. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper discusses opening opportunities for female pilot students at partner civilian universities. Related printed notes 89, 90 on PDF p. 55, 56.
rows.finding: Tsinghua identifies five women among the joint intake of 35 in 2019 and records a second female group in 2021. The 35 is the combined Tsinghua cohort and should not be substituted for the Air Force-wide number of women recruited.
evidence: Tsinghua University’s 2019 female pilot cadet intake release
Tsinghua University’s 2021 retrospective on dual-registration cohorts

rows.source: Distinction between the original Tiangong laboratory and the later space station
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The earlier Shenzhou mission boarded Tiangong 1, described as a space station in the report. Related printed notes 104 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The flight and programme histories confirm rendezvous with Tiangong 1. Official later documents distinguish that experimental target or laboratory from the later permanently inhabited station programme. Use the specific programme and hardware name.
evidence: Shenzhou 9 programme archive, post-flight crew and mission account
State Council archive of the 2016 space white paper
Full text of the 2021 space white paper, issued January 2022

rows.source: Chronology of the first women’s aviation cohort
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 19. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study starts its first female aviation cohort in 1951.
rows.finding: The official history dates the assignment of 55 trainees to April 1951 and the subsequent public flight event to March 1952. Training and public debut are separately dated.
evidence: Official military history of the first women’s aviation cohort
PLA Daily historical reconstruction of the 1951 cohort

rows.source: Count of first-cohort aviation trainees versus pilots
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 19. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The first intake is presented as a cohort of female aviators with assignments across aviation roles.
rows.finding: The official histories identify 55 aviation trainees overall and a flight student subset of 14 in the first cohort. The intake count is broader than the count training as pilots.
evidence: Official military history of the first women’s aviation cohort
PLA Daily historical reconstruction of the 1951 cohort

rows.source: Public flight event and later reception in 1952
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 20. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper relates the first cohort’s public event to recognition by state leaders.
rows.finding: The official record places the public flight event on 8 March and the reception by Mao and other leaders on 24 March. These are distinct appearances.
evidence: Official military history of the first women’s aviation cohort
PLA Daily historical reconstruction of the 1951 cohort

rows.source: Specialties in the second women’s aviation cohort
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 20. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The passage calls all 44 people pilots before listing 21 pilots, 17 navigators and six communicators. Related printed notes 65 on PDF p. 55.
rows.finding: The listed categories sum to 44 aviation trainees, with 21 counted in the pilot category. The original cohort source is required to corroborate the counts independently, while the wording error is clear from the breakdown.
evidence: CASI Females in the PLA Air Force original study (GovInfo PDF)
PLA Daily historical reconstruction of the 1951 cohort

rows.source: Bachelor’s qualification for sixth cohort and conflicting month
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 21. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper dates graduation to March 1993 and calls the sixth group the first receiving a bachelor’s qualification. Related printed notes 71 on PDF p. 55.
rows.finding: The Air Force’s later historical timeline gives August 1993 for the sixth cohort’s graduation and confirms the first bachelor’s-level group. The differing months may refer to distinct milestones. The contemporaneous ceremony record is still needed.
evidence: Air Force official chronology and thirteenth cohort notice

rows.source: Eleventh cohort starting strength and reference year
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 23. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes a 35-person cohort entering the aviation university in 2017. Related printed notes 87 on PDF p. 55.
rows.finding: The Air Force cohort chronology confirms the broad succession. A contemporaneous 2017 intake release with the named count is needed to distinguish admissions from eventual graduates.
evidence: Air Force official chronology and thirteenth cohort notice
CASI Females in the PLA Air Force original study (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Admission number for the thirteenth cohort
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 23. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study gives 23 entrants for the 2021 group.
rows.finding: The contemporary official Air Force account specifies 23 entrants in the thirteenth cohort. The number refers to selections at entry rather than the subset entering university partnerships.
evidence: Air Force official chronology and thirteenth cohort notice

rows.source: Attested first female PLAAF division commander
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 26. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report identifies Cheng Xiaojian as the first woman appointed an Air Force division commander.
rows.finding: The official retrospective credits Cheng with the first female division command in the PLAAF. For the exact appointment day the full original appointment announcement would provide finer precision.
evidence: Beijing Women’s Federation retrospective on first female aviators

rows.source: Geographic limits of the recruitment sample
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 17. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper describes patterns using selective provincial recruitment reports.
rows.finding: Table 2 explicitly combines records from selected jurisdictions and years. It even includes a 2009 Yunnan row outside the main 2012–2016 window. The results are descriptive of that sample.
evidence: CASI Females in the PLA Air Force original study (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Evaluation versus recruitment in a representative table row
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 17. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper’s Ningxia entry calculates a share from women evaluated rather than final entrants.
rows.finding: The printed row gives 240 evaluated of 1,190 registered in 2013, or 20.17 percent rounded to 20.2 percent. It carries an evaluation label that should follow the figure in later use.
evidence: CASI Females in the PLA Air Force original study (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Published female share for the Shaanxi registration sample
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 17. Extracted claim in paraphrase. One row relates 25 successful female candidates to the corresponding total of 684 recruits.
rows.finding: The table’s division gives 3.65 percent, displayed as 3.7 percent. This is an arithmetic check on the tabulated Shaanxi record. It provides no independent national estimate.
evidence: CASI Females in the PLA Air Force original study (GovInfo PDF)

evidence: The U.S., China, and Artificial Intelligence Competition Factors

rows.source: Substantive argument and evidentiary scope
rows.usage: Supplied PDF pp. 9–11. Extracted argument in paraphrase.
rows.finding: Sullivan asks whether competition over AI norms is inherently zero-sum and examines values, cohesion, influence and legitimacy. Standards-setting and participation in international institutions are part of that comparison. An official national objective can confirm the priority as of its issue date while its achievement depends on other evidence. This reading establishes the scope of the authors’ argument. Its interpretation and broader empirical inferences need case-specific primary evidence.
evidence: The U.S., China, and Artificial Intelligence Competition Factors

rows.source: State Council, New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan
rows.usage: PDF pp. 9–10, comparative framework. Independent policy comparison.
rows.finding: The 2017 State Council notice sets staged objectives, including a 2030 leadership ambition. It confirms a national policy priority and a timeline. Sullivan’s judgment about norms competition draws on a wider framework and cannot be established from this plan alone.
evidence: State Council, New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan

rows.source: Framing of U.S.–China competition in the 2017 NSS
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper dates the U.S. strategy’s explicit competitive framing to December 2017. Related printed notes 1 on PDF p. 73.
rows.finding: The introductory pages describe China and Russia as challengers to U.S. interests. The same strategy treats competition as compatible with seeking cooperation. This supports the attribution and shows that the framing alone does not establish an exclusively zero-sum relationship.
evidence: December 2017 U.S. National Security Strategy, Department of Defense archive

rows.source: Role of universities in the AI plan’s research agenda
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report identifies universities as the focus of the 2018 education ministry plan for basic and applied research. Related printed notes 19 on PDF p. 74.
rows.finding: The ministry notice explicitly implements the broader State Council plan through higher education. Its first task is strengthening basic theory and it also calls for transfer and application. The mandate applies to the university plan; the national plan assigns work to other actors too.
evidence: Ministry of Education AI action plan for universities, April 2018
State Council New Generation AI Development Plan, July 2017

rows.source: Pan Yunhe’s role in the cited AI education material
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper attributes the two-power framing to Pan and labels his statement with the title of the AI action plan. Related printed notes 117, 118 on PDF p. 82.
rows.finding: The June 8 agenda lists Pan as a presenter on the plan. The published plan is Ministry of Education document 教技〔2018〕3号, signed in April. Neither the agenda nor the formal plan alone verifies the exact quote. The June briefing transcript is needed for the spoken wording.
evidence: Ministry of Education June 8 briefing agenda with Pan Yunhe
Ministry of Education AI action plan for universities, April 2018

rows.source: University action plan’s three main policy functions
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 29. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study characterizes the plan as spanning research innovation, training and commercial or applied diffusion. Related printed notes 130 on PDF p. 84.
rows.finding: The three relevant task headings are redesign of the university innovation system, improvement of talent development, and application or demonstration of results. These headings support the report’s characterization. Retention effects require a separate evaluation.
evidence: Ministry of Education AI action plan for universities, April 2018

rows.source: Everest Plan’s basic research remit
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 29. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The Everest Plan is a separate higher education initiative centered on basic research. Related printed notes 138 on PDF p. 85.
rows.finding: The signed July 18, 2018 notice explicitly assigns basic research priorities and organizational measures to universities. The December 2020 education ministry briefing describes early implementation. The action plan for AI in higher education is a separate April 2018 issuance.
evidence: Ministry of Education Everest Plan for basic research
December 2020 Ministry of Education briefing report

rows.source: Dating the Everest Plan announcement
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 29. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report treats the plan as an education ministry policy from 2018. Related printed notes 138 on PDF p. 85.
rows.finding: The instrument is signed July 18. The ministry metadata records July 19 as generation date and the public archive locator is August 1. Use the signed date for issuance and note the difference where a source cites the posting date.
evidence: Ministry of Education Everest Plan for basic research

rows.source: Online and offline platform oversight
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 17. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The author cites the platform economy opinion for coordinated oversight across online and offline activity. Related printed notes 43 on PDF p. 76.
rows.finding: The guidance calls for overall coordination of internet regulation, improvement of laws, and integrated online and offline supervision. This supports the attributed prescription. It does not measure the extent to which platform operations changed after issuance.
evidence: State Council General Office 2019 platform economy guidance

rows.source: Social-service provision in the platform guidance
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 20. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The guidance invokes online medical services and expanding access to higher-quality services. Related printed notes 69 on PDF p. 79.
rows.finding: The provision explicitly supports participation in internet-based health and other services and improved education and medical network infrastructure. This confirms the policy’s stated intent. A health outcomes or access dataset is needed to test the result.
evidence: State Council General Office 2019 platform economy guidance

rows.source: Platform guidance and industrial modernization
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 38. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The opinion is invoked as evidence of a policy link between platform development and digital production. Related printed notes 241 on PDF p. 91.
rows.finding: The General Office describes platform activity as an organizing form for upgrading industry. It supports integration with production and services. The policy’s scope is broader than AI and it does not quantify adopted industrial applications.

rows.source: Information covered by China’s Data Security Law
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 24. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The description says data includes information recorded electronically or by other means. Related printed notes 103 on PDF p. 81.

rows.source: Limits of the Schrems II privacy ruling
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 24. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper invokes the 2020 EU court ruling as a restriction on U.S. data access.
rows.finding: The court invalidated the Privacy Shield adequacy decision on July 16, 2020, while preserving the standard contractual clauses decision subject to safeguards. This is a ruling on legal bases for transfers, with an important difference between the two mechanisms.
evidence: Court of Justice release on the July 16, 2020 Schrems II judgment

rows.source: Wrong edition cited for the 2014 integrated circuits outline
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 36. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The text dates the integrated circuit industry outline to 2014. The note links a government document whose locator is August 2020. Related printed notes 216 on PDF p. 90.

Ministry of Finance copy of the 2020 integrated circuit and software notice

rows.source: China Standards 2035 as a research project
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 44. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study distinguishes the proposed China Standards 2035 work from a public standalone national policy. Related printed notes 298 on PDF p. 95.

The published October 2021 instrument is titled National Standardization Development Outline. Keep the project and final instrument separate.
evidence: Standardization Administration announcement launching the China Standards 2035 project

rows.source: Scope of the 2035 standardization objective
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 45. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report’s discussion treats research on standards as a step toward a national strategy and international engagement. Related printed notes 299 on PDF p. 95.

rows.source: Mandate of the ITU environmental efficiency focus group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The group studies standardization needs for AI and other technologies in environmental efficiency. Related printed notes 312 on PDF p. 96.

rows.source: CAICT publication and issuing context
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 60. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study refers to a September 2020 conference paper by CAICT on AI governance. Related printed notes 417, 419 on PDF p. 104.

Its title and issue date differ from the paper cited in the note. The September 28 conference edition must be located to verify the quotation and exact attribution.

rows.source: Cyber sovereignty as the study’s reading of CAICT
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 61. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper draws a cyber-sovereignty implication from CAICT’s emphasis on governments. Related printed notes 419, 420 on PDF p. 104.

evidence: CAICT-hosted December 2020 report on global AI governance
MOST publication of the 2019 AI governance principles

rows.source: PwC’s job displacement and creation figures are scenarios
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 21. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The article gives 26 percent displacement and 38 percent creation, for a net increase of 12 percent. Related printed notes 76 on PDF p. 79.

rows.source: Time horizon of the PwC China employment estimate
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 21. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report groups PwC’s China result with a U.S. prediction over fifteen years. Related printed notes 76 on PDF p. 79.
rows.finding: The 2018 PwC work models the two decades to 2037. Label that horizon explicitly. Its estimates should be associated with the company’s scenario rather than inferred from an independent U.S. time frame.
evidence: PwC original 2018 report, The Impact of AI on Jobs in China

rows.source: The Future of Work programme was an NSF research solicitation
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 21. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper uses NSF’s programme as an example of research on technology and employment.
rows.finding: The 2019 solicitation defines the Core Research programme and its interdisciplinary remit. It supports the programme attribution and public-research role.
evidence: National Science Foundation 2019 Future of Work solicitation

rows.source: Definition of origin for the selected AI researcher cohort
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes China as the source of almost one third of top-tier AI talent. Related printed notes 119 on PDF p. 82.
rows.finding: The underlying 2020 tracker uses where selected researchers received undergraduate degrees as the origin measure and defines its sample from a 2019 research conference. About 29 percent is a share of this sample.
evidence: Paulson Institute announcement of the original Global AI Talent Tracker
World Bank original data for the 2021 World Development Report

rows.source: Where China-trained AI researchers worked in the 2019 sample
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors give the U.S. and China employment distributions of the China-trained subset as 56 and 34 percent. Related printed notes 119 on PDF p. 82.
rows.finding: The original tracker and accompanying analysis give those shares using its 2019 cohort. The denominator is the subset whose undergraduate education was in China.
evidence: Paulson Institute announcement of the original Global AI Talent Tracker
MacroPolo original 2020 analysis of the talent tracker

rows.source: Scale and meaning of the reported AI talent deficit
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper cites an estimate of more than five million people in unmet AI talent demand. Related printed notes 123 on PDF p. 83.
rows.finding: The cited discussion and the official education plan establish that talent shortages were a policy concern. A defined employment population and reproducible supply and vacancy series are needed to validate the numerical estimate.
evidence: Science Net cited article on China’s AI talent challenges
Education Ministry university AI innovation plan

rows.source: Base-year increase in basic research spending
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 30. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper reports 22.5 percent year-on-year growth in China’s basic research expenditure in 2019. Related printed notes 150 on PDF p. 86.
rows.finding: The official R&D communiqué gives 133.56 billion yuan for basic research and a 22.5 percent increase over 2018. The data cover all sectors within the national statistical programme.
evidence: National Bureau of Statistics 2019 R&D expenditure communiqué

rows.source: Share of basic research in national R&D expenditure
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 30. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The article puts basic research spending at six percent of total R&D in 2019. Related printed notes 150 on PDF p. 86.
rows.finding: The bulletin reports 133.56 billion yuan basic research over total domestic R&D of 2,214.36 billion yuan. The percentage follows the official classification by research activity.
evidence: National Bureau of Statistics 2019 R&D expenditure communiqué

rows.source: Four initial open innovation platform assignments
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 33. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper dates the initial set of national AI open innovation platforms to 2017 before further additions. Related printed notes 173 on PDF p. 88.
rows.finding: The original launch release names four enterprise-led platforms and their specified civilian application domains. Later releases can be used to track additions without retroactively changing the initial roster.
evidence: Chinese government original announcement of four AI platform leads
MOST briefing transcript on platform launch

rows.source: Expansion of the national open platform roster in 2019
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 33. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper reports that additions in August 2019 took the roster to 15. Related printed notes 173 on PDF p. 88.

evidence: Contemporary coverage of the Ministry’s ten additional platform designations
MOST national open innovation platform work guidelines

rows.source: Subject specialisation and openness obligations for AI platforms
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 33. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper says platform hosts take responsibility for a designated area and make resources available more widely. Related printed notes 174 on PDF p. 88.
rows.finding: The original guidelines organise platform construction by application field and call for resource sharing and external services. The requirement specifies programme responsibilities.
evidence: MOST national open innovation platform work guidelines

rows.source: SME service objective versus the 96 percent sector statistic
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 33. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper cites the proportion of high-tech enterprises classified as small, medium or micro to contextualise the platforms. Related printed notes 175 on PDF p. 88.
rows.finding: The platform construction guidance supports SME service as an objective. The 96 percent figure needs the corresponding enterprise registry, size definitions and reference year.
evidence: MOST national open innovation platform work guidelines

rows.source: Two places identified as early AI innovation pilot zones
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 37. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper identifies both cities as early pilot areas. Related printed notes 225 on PDF p. 90.
rows.finding: MOST published a Shanghai approval letter and its Beijing work review identifies the Beijing pilot programme. These records concern local experimental zones, distinct from enterprise-led open platforms.
evidence: MOST written approval of the Shanghai AI innovation pilot

rows.source: Reported number of planned national AI innovation pilot zones
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 37. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report treats 18 likely additional pilots as an expansion from two already reported in 2020. Related printed notes 225 on PDF p. 90.
rows.finding: The updated guideline sets a national ambition of approximately 20 zones by 2023. Eighteen additional is an inference from the two named in the paragraph and should be described as such.
evidence: MOST revised national AI pilot-zone guidance
MOST written approval of the Shanghai AI innovation pilot

rows.source: Institutional role of the OCEANIS collaboration forum
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 47. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper says the forum facilitates collaboration on ethical standards for autonomous and intelligent systems. Related printed notes 325 on PDF p. 97.
rows.finding: The official forum description places the initiative in standards cooperation and best-practice exchange. It supports the claim about purpose and leaves national legal adoption to other records.

rows.source: Proposed status of the Multilateral AI Research Institute
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 47. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper describes the institute as an NSCAI recommendation supporting scientific exchanges. Related printed notes 326 on PDF p. 97.
rows.finding: The final report proposes the institute and names its collaborative aims. The citation supports a recommendation in 2021 rather than an operational organisation.
evidence: NSCAI final report federal repository edition

rows.source: Public attitudes to AI in the five Asian publics cited by Pew
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 20. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report paraphrases Pew as finding 60 percent positive views across selected Asian publics. Related printed notes 66 on PDF p. 79.
rows.finding: Pew reports separate percentages of 72 for Singapore, 69 for South Korea, 66 for Taiwan and 65 for Japan. India also recorded 67 percent. The citation establishes at least roughly two-thirds in each named public rather than a pooled 60 percent.
evidence: Pew Research Center, 2020 Global Attitudes survey publication

rows.source: Geographic and temporal scope of the Pew comparison
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 20. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report compares attitudes in Asian publics with attitudes in the U.S., Canada and parts of Europe. Related printed notes 66 on PDF p. 79.
rows.finding: Fieldwork covered 20 publics in late 2019 and early 2020. U.S. and Canadian results were below half on the AI question, but several European publics were above half. These comparisons describe survey respondents at that date and include no mainland China result.
evidence: Pew Research Center, 2020 Global Attitudes survey publication

rows.source: Which automated decisions are covered by GDPR Article 22
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 24. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes the EU regulation as imposing significant constraints on the use of AI. Related printed notes 102 on PDF p. 81.
rows.finding: Article 22 concerns solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects. It contains exceptions and safeguards. The statutory claim supports a restriction on specified decisions rather than a broad prohibition on machine learning.

rows.source: Place of smart-campus policy in China Education Modernization 2035
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The author treats the education modernization plan as a policy basis for using AI and digital tools in education. Related printed notes 120 on PDF p. 83.
rows.finding: The February 2019 release calls for smart campuses, integrated teaching and administration platforms and changes to talent development. It establishes the education-wide objective. The 2018 higher education AI plan has a more specific research mandate.
evidence: Ministry of Education archive of China Education Modernization 2035

rows.source: China’s university-quality ranking in the 2020 Global Innovation Index
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 29. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report attributes a third-place university-quality rank to China in the 2020 index. Related printed notes 131 on PDF p. 84.
rows.finding: WIPO identifies third place for this indicator and names Tsinghua, Peking and Fudan in the global top 50 used for it. The third-place figure is an indicator ranking. Overall innovation is measured separately.
evidence: WIPO, Global Innovation Index 2020, China country profile

rows.source: Overall 2020 innovation ranking versus output measures
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 29. Extracted claim in paraphrase. China ranked 14th overall in the 2020 index despite performing differently on individual indicators. Related printed notes 135 on PDF p. 84.
rows.finding: The 2020 country profile gives 14th overall and shows separate input and output ranks. Use the overall rank for the composite and the named indicators when discussing patenting, institutions or universities.
evidence: WIPO, Global Innovation Index 2020, China country profile

rows.source: Corporate research ranking comes from an EU scoreboard
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 36. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The 2020 list includes 536 firms based in China and 775 in the United States. Related printed notes 212 on PDF p. 90.
rows.finding: The primary JRC scoreboard reproduces both counts and covers corporate financial data for 2019, across 2,500 firms. The report’s reference to the Global Innovation Index confuses two products. The 536 and 775 are counts of companies, not shares of spending.
evidence: European Commission Joint Research Centre, 2020 industrial research investment scoreboard

rows.source: Definition and ranking of the 17 science and technology clusters
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 37. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper attributes 17 clusters and the Shenzhen–Hong Kong–Guangzhou and Beijing rankings to WIPO. Related printed notes 224 on PDF p. 90.
rows.finding: The China profile identifies 17 and ranks the two named clusters second and fourth. These are measured geographic clusters under the index’s criteria. They are distinct from the policy-designated pilot zones mentioned nearby.
evidence: WIPO, Global Innovation Index 2020, China country profile

rows.source: Mandate of the ITU–WHO health focus group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report treats the focus group as a standardization forum for evaluating health applications of AI. Related printed notes 310 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: ITU records creation in 2018 and a joint assessment-method mandate with WHO. The group’s work concerned evaluating solutions, including diagnosis and triage. The record does not certify individual clinical products.
evidence: ITU and WHO Focus Group on Artificial Intelligence for Health
ITU registry of concluded standardization focus groups

rows.source: Shan Xu’s role in the ITU health emergency group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report identifies a CAICT representative as a co-chair of a COVID health emergency group. Related printed notes 311 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: The official roster credits Shan Xu of CAICT and Ana R. Cinnamond of PAHO/WHO as the two co-chairs. This confirms a co-chair position at subgroup level, distinct from leadership of the parent body.
evidence: ITU health emergency ad hoc group terms and management roster

rows.source: China Telecommunications’ seat in the disaster management focus group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The author identifies Wang as a vice-chair in ITU’s disaster management group. Related printed notes 313 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: ITU records Yan Chuan Wang of China Telecommunications Corporation as one of several vice-chairs under chair Monique Kuglitsch. The appointment supports participation and provides no evidence of unilateral control of the outputs.
evidence: ITU disaster management focus group mandate and management roster
ITU registry of concluded standardization focus groups

rows.source: Institutional purpose of the ITU driving focus group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes a specialist group for AI safety in autonomous and assisted driving. Related printed notes 314 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: The terms distinguish behavioural evaluation and standardization in driving from vehicle approval. The source confirms the group’s remit, which is separate from the report’s evidence about national gains from participation.
evidence: ITU autonomous and assisted driving focus group public record

rows.source: Attributed Chinese vice-chair in the driving focus group
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report says Zhang Yuan held a vice-chair role in the driving focus group. Related printed notes 314 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: The archived focus group and parent registry identify the work and period. The public page checked does not establish that name and role combination. A dated meeting report or management roster is needed, including whether the role was with the focus group or a workstream.
evidence: ITU autonomous and assisted driving focus group public record
ITU registry of concluded standardization focus groups

rows.source: Focus group outputs versus ITU recommendations
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report links the machine-learning focus group to standards work on future networks. Related printed notes 315 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: The registry dates establishment to November 2017 and lists draft specifications sent from the group to Study Group 13. It separately identifies recommendations based on that work. Distinguish the drafts produced by the focus group from the recommendations adopted by the study group.
evidence: ITU focus group on machine learning for future networks

rows.source: Meng Wei’s specific machine-learning working group appointment
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study attributes leadership of working group 3 to a ZTE representative. Related printed notes 315 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: The group’s archive confirms its active period and outputs. The visible public page gives no matching dated chair appointment for this name. The cited working-group meeting record is needed to check the institutional affiliation and title.
evidence: ITU focus group on machine learning for future networks

rows.source: Cisco and ZTE were 2020 ITU challenge sponsors
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper uses the presence of U.S. and Chinese firms as an example of participation in the same forum. Related printed notes 316 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: ITU’s event page lists both firms as bronze sponsors, distinct from the organizer, gold sponsor and regional hosts. The sponsors’ names establish joint participation in the event rather than a bilateral standard-setting agreement.

rows.source: Qiang Zhang’s precise appointment and institutional affiliation
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report identifies Qiang Zhang as the Chinese participant in leadership of a quantum network focus group. Related printed notes 317 on PDF p. 97.
rows.finding: The group’s roster identifies Qiang Zhang of USTC as one of three co-chairs. Several other members from affiliated organizations held other posts. The roster supports the exact title rather than a sole national representative role.

rows.source: Name discrepancy for the quantum focus group workstream chair
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 46. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The body identifies Ma Zhongchao as a workstream chair. Related printed notes 319 on PDF p. 97.
rows.finding: The ITU roster records Zhangchao Ma of CAS Quantum Network for working group 2. The paper’s note also uses Zhangchao. This is distinct from Jiajun Ma, who is on the same roster as a vice-chair.
evidence: ITU quantum information technology for networks focus group, roster

rows.source: Multilateral membership and dating the RCEP example
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 58. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study cites RCEP as an example of engagement through regional institutions. Related printed notes 402 on PDF p. 103.
rows.finding: The November 15, 2020 leaders’ statement records the 15 participating governments and the signature at an ASEAN summit. This verifies China’s participation and the multilateral context. Relative influence requires different evidence.
evidence: Joint leaders’ November 2020 statement announcing the RCEP signing

rows.source: Substance and provenance of Blinken’s Anchorage formulation
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 70. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The conclusion quotes Blinken’s tripartite description of the U.S. relationship with China. Related printed notes 488 on PDF p. 108.

evidence: State Department transcript of the March 18, 2021 Anchorage opening session

paper_memo.memo_title: The U.S., China, and Artificial Intelligence Competition Factors

sections.heading: Context and core argument
sections.body: Sullivan asks whether competition over AI norms is inherently zero-sum and examines values, cohesion, influence and legitimacy. Standards-setting and participation in international institutions are part of that comparison. An official national objective can confirm the priority as of its issue date while its achievement depends on other evidence.

sections.heading: How to read the evidence
sections.body: Compare policy language and research indicators on their stated time horizons. Keep national targets separate from observed outcomes.

sections.heading: Citation and claim checks
sections.body: **State Council, New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan.** PDF pp. 9–10, comparative framework. Independent policy comparison. The 2017 State Council notice sets staged objectives, including a 2030 leadership ambition. It confirms a national policy priority and a timeline. Sullivan’s judgment about norms competition draws on a wider framework and cannot be established from this plan alone.

rows.source: Civilian product scope of CASC’s corporate remit

rows.source: Definition and scope of the industrial study

CASIC executive’s 2016 interview on corporate history

rows.source: Publication attribution and edition
rows.usage: Supplied PDF cover and imprint, PDF pp. 1–2. Bibliographic comparison.
rows.finding: The supplied PDF front matter names Kenneth W. Allen, Cristina L. Garafola and identifies China Aerospace Studies Institute as publisher. Edition or release date is recorded as April 12, 2021.
evidence: 70 Years of the PLA Air Force (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Substantive argument and evidentiary scope
rows.usage: Supplied PDF pp. 14–16. Extracted argument in paraphrase.
rows.finding: The book combines institutional history with chapters on organization, personnel, education, training and military diplomacy. The introduction explicitly defines the project around the service’s organizational and human dimensions. It offers longitudinal context for reading Allen’s narrower studies of commanders and women’s careers. This reading establishes the scope of the authors’ argument. Its interpretation and broader empirical inferences need case-specific primary evidence.
evidence: 70 Years of the PLA Air Force (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: First twelve Zhuhai shows and the exception to the even-year pattern
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 320. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report counts twelve exhibitions on the regular even-year schedule through its period. Related printed notes 1761 on PDF p. 466.
rows.finding: The organizer dates the first show to 1996 and the twelfth to November 2018. Its 2021 announcement identifies the next show as the thirteenth. Use the even-year regularity for the first twelve and date subsequent editions separately.
evidence: Zhuhai air show organizer’s retrospective and 12th exhibition announcement
Zhuhai air show organizer’s August 2021 press release for the 13th exhibition

rows.source: Air Force headquarters founding date
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 38. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors date the formation of the Air Force leading organization to November 11, 1949. Related printed notes 14 on PDF p. 407.
rows.finding: The ministry’s historical account uses November 11 for establishment of headquarters. Civil aviation records document a separate administrative decision days earlier. The date belongs to the formal Air Force institution rather than the beginning of all Communist aviation work.
evidence: Ministry of National Defense historical account of the foundation of the Air Force
CAAC history of early civil aviation administration

rows.source: Northeast Aviation School as precursor to the formal Air Force
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 37. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chapter traces Communist aviation education to a school in the northeast before formal establishment in 1949.
rows.finding: The ministry retrospective describes the school’s earlier origins and its role in developing a first aviation cohort. The 1949 account explicitly describes personnel draws from that school. This supports a predecessor relationship rather than an identical institution.
evidence: Ministry of National Defense history of the Northeast Aviation School
Ministry of National Defense historical account of the foundation of the Air Force

rows.source: September 2015 announcement versus implemented personnel reduction
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 61. Extracted claim in paraphrase. Xi announced a 300,000-person reduction on September 3, 2015.
rows.finding: The contemporaneous official transcript specifies the 300,000 figure. It confirms an announced target, with no breakdown by officers and other personnel. The report’s half-officer statement requires additional implementation evidence.
evidence: September 3, 2015 speech announcing reduction of 300,000 personnel

rows.source: Rank and grade are separate classification axes
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 62. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book treats billet grades and commissioned ranks as related classification schemes with different meanings.
rows.finding: The companion CASI study’s Appendix 3 and Table 6 use separate grade and rank columns with multiple possible ranks for several grades. This supports the reading of the historical personnel tables. It does not establish that post-2021 rules retained the same emphasis.
evidence: CASI publisher record for the commanders study (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Service chiefs’ CMC membership changed in the 2000s
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 66. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book identifies Air Force commanders Xu Qiliang and Ma Xiaotian as CMC members. Related printed notes 83, 84 on PDF p. 410.
rows.finding: The official Xu chronology verifies his 2007 Party CMC appointment and 2008 state CMC appointment. It supports the Xu case and shows that an appointment to one body does not set the date for the other. Ma’s separate appointment instrument remains necessary for full comparison.
evidence: 2018 official biographies of the two state CMC vice chairmen

rows.source: Wei Fenghe’s transition to minister in 2018
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 67. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book identifies Wei Fenghe’s ministerial appointment as a separate step from his prior service command.
rows.finding: The white paper confirms the institutional pattern of recent military reforms. The paper names the first session of the 13th NPC as the appointment context. The individual appointment list or decision is still needed for the precise date and continuity of CMC membership.
evidence: SCIO 2019 national defence white paper, strategy section

rows.source: Nationwide five-percent ceiling versus documented university variation
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 176. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chapter sets a general five-percent female intake ceiling for the Defense Student programme.
rows.finding: The later female personnel report says the apparent national ceiling was applied inconsistently and cites Peking University as an exception. Both CASI works share an author. The national rule and the campus-specific 2015 notice must be checked to determine whether the difference reflects an exception or unlike denominators.
evidence: GovInfo copy of the CASI academy study
CASI publisher summary of the female personnel study (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Defense Student stipend components and later increase
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 176. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The original stipend is described as 5,000 yuan per year, split between tuition and living expenses, rising later to 10,000 yuan.
rows.finding: The cited decomposition of 3,000 and 2,000 sums to 5,000 yuan. The companion study and Hunan release verify programme scope and intake closure but do not supply a dated stipend schedule. The distribution of the later amount remains unresolved.
evidence: GovInfo copy of the CASI academy study
Hunan government admissions report for the 2017 cycle

rows.source: Civilian employee categories changed after the book’s period
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 195. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The 2017 framework used management and specialist technical work categories. Related printed notes 835 on PDF p. 434.
rows.finding: The 2017 Article 2 description names management and professional technical work. The 2022 revision also explicitly includes technical skill functions. This corroborates the historical label and supplies a dated update for later use.
evidence: 2017 civilian personnel regulations in the Ministry of Justice historical archive
2022 revised PLA civilian personnel regulations published by the ministry

rows.source: Formation of the Ministry of Veterans Affairs
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 199. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book dates the creation of a separate veterans affairs ministry to the 2018 institutional reorganization.
rows.finding: The March 13 plan explanation proposes consolidating responsibilities from civilian ministries and CMC departments. The ministry’s own report dates establishment to April 2018. The two records distinguish the proposal from formation.
evidence: Veterans Affairs Ministry account of its formation and remit
Explanation of the March 2018 State Council reorganization plan to the NPC

rows.source: Translation of professional military education terminology
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 202. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors explain their use of an English analytical label for several Chinese categories. Related printed notes 872 on PDF p. 436.
rows.finding: The academy report distinguishes degree and position-oriented education. NIDS discusses professional education in a separate continuing education section. These records support retaining the Chinese term where cited because the English label can group different programme types.
evidence: GovInfo copy of the CASI academy study
NIDS China Security Report 2022, Chinese edition, Table 3-1 and its sources

rows.source: Air Force institutions in the June 2017 list
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 214. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chapter’s 10-school set includes the three flight academies and an NCO school.
rows.finding: The decade history and the CASI academy report agree on ten names for the 2017 Air Force grouping. Table 3-1 of the Japanese study reproduces the grouping, partly using CASI. It is a dated count and contains one explicitly titled NCO school.
evidence: Ministry of National Defense, June 29, 2017 academy roster preserved by Xinhua
GovInfo copy of the CASI academy study
NIDS China Security Report 2022, Chinese edition, Table 3-1 and its sources

rows.source: International exchange coverage among Air Force schools
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 214. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors report that four of the ten schools engaged in international exchanges.
rows.finding: The companion profiles distinguish exchanges by institution and the external review describes selected educational contacts. Neither supplies a consistent all-institutions activity register for the same years. The four-school count remains a literature-based observation.
evidence: GovInfo copy of the CASI academy study
NIDS China Security Report 2022, Chinese edition, Table 3-1 and its sources

rows.source: Dual-registration phases at Tsinghua
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 230. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book describes civilian university study followed by Air Force university study in the dual-enrollment model.
rows.finding: Tsinghua’s 2013 admissions description confirms the joint programme, and its retrospective describes dual registration and a three-plus-one degree model. The institutional arrangement does not report every student’s completion.
evidence: Tsinghua University’s 2021 retrospective on dual-registration cohorts

rows.source: Start of joint education versus start of dual registration
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 229. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study treats the pilot programme and later expansion as stages of a joint educational initiative.
rows.finding: The 2013 release distinguishes cooperation beginning in 2011, joint recruitment in 2012 and dual-registration admissions in 2013. The retrospective uses 2011 for the broader programme. Preserve these dates by milestone.
evidence: Tsinghua University’s 2021 retrospective on dual-registration cohorts

rows.source: Forecast horizon and change over time
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 342. Extracted claim in paraphrase. Chapter 8 presents prospective judgments through 2029.
rows.finding: The chapter labels the ten-year horizon as predictions. The referenced closure provides an example of programme change, while the later 2025 announcement documents additional reforms at other institutions. Cite a later outcome source when using individual forecasts as retrospective evidence.
evidence: Hunan government admissions report for the 2017 cycle
Ministry of National Defense announcement on three new schools

rows.source: Author translations versus official titles in English references
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 375. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors use citation typography to identify unofficial English renderings of Chinese titles.
rows.finding: The formatting statement on PDF p. 375 specifies brackets for author-translated book titles followed by the Chinese. Appendix F on p. 384 retains original Chinese titles. Cite that convention when reconciling apparently different titles, and match the Chinese name and edition.

rows.source: Enactment date of the PRC’s first Military Service Law
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 179. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The institutional history dates the law’s entry into force before its July 1955 discussion. Related printed notes 757 on PDF p. 432.
rows.finding: The legislative chronology places enactment of the first statute on 30 July 1955. Any December 1954 milestone needs its own contemporary instrument and should be described separately from the law’s adoption.
evidence: People’s Congress legislative history of the first Military Service Law
Official defence press on the service law’s legislative history

rows.source: Adoption and effective date of the replacement service law
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 180. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper dates NPC approval of the service law to May 1984. Related printed notes 761 on PDF p. 432.
rows.finding: The original law was adopted on 31 May 1984 and took effect on 1 October 1984. Both dates are available in the official legislative publications.
evidence: Education ministry archive of the 1984 statutory text
NPC Standing Committee Gazette of the revised 2021 Military Service Law

rows.source: Enactment and effect of the December 1998 amendment
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 181. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper dates effect of the late-1998 service law amendment to 1 January 1999. Related printed notes 769 on PDF p. 432.
rows.finding: The NPC standing committee adopted the amendment on 29 December 1998. The gazetted amendment applies from promulgation. The report may have conflated the statutory date with a separate implementation date.
evidence: State Council Gazette of the 1998 Military Service Law amendment
NPC Standing Committee Gazette of the revised 2021 Military Service Law

rows.source: Two-year service term in the 1998 statutory text
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 181. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes the change eliminating the old service-specific conscript periods. Related printed notes 769 on PDF p. 432.
rows.finding: The 1984 and amended texts show the change from differentiated periods in the old law to two years for active-duty conscript soldiers. The provision concerns that legal category.
evidence: Education ministry archive of the 1984 statutory text
State Council Gazette of the 1998 Military Service Law amendment

rows.source: Date of the third Military Service Law revision
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 185. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study dates passage of the 2011 amendment to October. Related printed notes 797 on PDF p. 433.
rows.finding: The current law’s legislative history and the 2011 decision date the third amendment to 29 October 2011. The printed legal history distinguishes the 2009 amendment and the 2021 full revision.
evidence: Official republication of the third Military Service Law amendment
NPC Standing Committee Gazette of the revised 2021 Military Service Law

rows.source: Legal basis for higher education resumption following service
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 186. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The text describes post-service educational preferences for students called to service.
rows.finding: The 2011 decision sets preservation of student status and allows resumption after release, with preferential treatment under relevant rules. The report's university-major detail depends on implementing education rules.
evidence: Official republication of the third Military Service Law amendment
NPC Standing Committee Gazette of the revised 2021 Military Service Law

rows.source: Scope of the reported five-percent state enterprise employment rule
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 186. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes a quota for former military personnel in all state enterprise hiring.
rows.finding: The 2011 amendment supplies resettlement duties and eligibility rules. The five-percent claim needs a dated implementing instrument to establish which employers, positions and beneficiary categories it covered.
evidence: Official republication of the third Military Service Law amendment
NPC Standing Committee Gazette of the revised 2021 Military Service Law

rows.source: Arithmetic and denominator in the 2018 aviation-school intake
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 174. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book gives 728 candidates and 379 admissions for the first school cohorts, with a 25 percent share.
rows.finding: The printed applicant and admission figures give 52.1 percent. If 25 percent refers to a share of all admissions, that denominator needs to be stated and checked against the source for the 2018 intake.
evidence: CASI 70 Years of the PLA Air Force original report (GovInfo PDF)
Defence Ministry 2019 pilot-selection release and earlier intake context

rows.source: Period covered by the biennial defence white paper description
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 336. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chapter quotes the 2010 annual report's description of a biennial publication pattern. Related printed notes 1845 on PDF p. 469.
rows.finding: The ministry’s retrospective lists the earlier even-year-labelled sequence, and the July 2019 white paper follows a different timing. Attribute the biennial observation to the 2010 report's period.
evidence: Defence Ministry retrospective on Chinese defence white papers
China’s National Defense in the New Era official white paper

rows.source: Institutional formation of the Strategic and Economic Dialogue
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 314. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book describes the 2009 consolidation of two earlier bilateral dialogue channels.
rows.finding: The 2009 U.S. records describe an inaugural dialogue with strategic and economic tracks and identify the preceding Senior and Strategic Economic Dialogues.
evidence: U.S.–China first-round Strategic and Economic Dialogue joint release
State Department backgrounder on formative U.S.–China dialogue

rows.source: First Strategic Security Dialogue under the S&ED
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 314. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book dates the launch of the security dialogue within the broader mechanism to 2011. Related printed notes 1715 on PDF p. 465.
rows.finding: The State Department’s strategic-track outcomes identify the inaugural Strategic Security Dialogue within the third round of the S&ED in May 2011.
evidence: U.S. State Department strategic track outcomes 2011

rows.source: Diplomatic and Security Dialogue within the 2017 architecture
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 314. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The history identifies the D&SD as a distinct 2017 diplomatic mechanism. Related printed notes 1716 on PDF p. 465.
rows.finding: The published November 2017 bilateral remarks identify the Diplomatic and Security Dialogue as one of four named high-level mechanisms agreed that year.
evidence: Published presidential remarks on the 2017 dialogue mechanisms

rows.source: Creation versus first implementation of the Joint Staff Dialogue
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 314. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book places the joint staff mechanism in 2017. Related printed notes 1717 on PDF p. 465.
rows.finding: The primary U.S. transcript discusses plans for the first dialogue in November 2017. The following annual report records 2017 agreement, providing a distinction between establishing a channel and scheduling meetings.
evidence: Published presidential remarks on the 2017 dialogue mechanisms
U.S. Defense Department 2018 annual China report

rows.source: Declared scope of non-war tasks in the 2019 defence white paper
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 318. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book groups humanitarian assistance and UN peacekeeping into the broad range of non-war and non-traditional security responsibilities. Related printed notes 1749 on PDF p. 466.
rows.finding: The official publications describe peacekeeping, humanitarian and disaster relief, and other international security activities. They establish the declared responsibilities and use different headings for their presentation.
evidence: China’s National Defense in the New Era official white paper
State Council 30 years of UN peacekeeping white paper

rows.source: Institutional participation in early UN peacekeeping
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 318. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chapter describes the PLA’s broader participation alongside a much narrower Air Force role.
rows.finding: The official peacekeeping history documents the PLA starting with five military observers to UNTSO in April 1990 and then using different personnel and unit contributions. The aggregate national history provides no exhaustive service-by-service participation register.
evidence: State Council 30 years of UN peacekeeping white paper

rows.source: Evidence required for the historical Air Force peacekeeping exception
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 318. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study describes 2016 transport support as the one Air Force exception in its period.
rows.finding: China’s white paper records national contributions to South Sudan. A service-tagged transport record and a comprehensive historical personnel roster are needed to substantiate both the reported airlift and the exclusivity claim.
evidence: State Council 30 years of UN peacekeeping white paper

rows.source: Xiangshan Forum first iteration and convening institution
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 319. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chapter presents the forum as a continuing security dialogue that predates its listed recent editions.
rows.finding: The organiser’s chronology dates the start to 2006 and identifies the China Association of Military Science as founder of a track-two platform. Later co-sponsorship is a separate change.

rows.source: Diplomatic level of the Xiangshan Forum after 2014
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 319. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chronology describes the forum’s widening participation and official engagement.
rows.finding: The organiser describes the fifth forum in 2014 as a shift to track 1.5, with wider participation including officials and nongovernmental attendees. This is the organiser’s own classification.

rows.source: Beijing designation of the eighth forum
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 319. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chapter treats the October 2018 event as the eighth edition of the same forum. Related printed notes 1756 on PDF p. 466.
rows.finding: The organiser specifies continuity from the Xiangshan Forum and identifies 2018 as the year the Beijing designation was adopted. Its official event record identifies the eighth edition.
evidence: PLA Daily contemporary coverage of the eighth forum

rows.source: Most-visited country count in the diplomacy chapter
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 321. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The narrative names Pakistan as the most visited destination and gives 10 visits.
rows.finding: Table 7-1 lists nine Pakistan visit years, with no duplicate year shown for that country. It presently supports the ordering but leaves a one-visit discrepancy with the narrative. An itinerary or omitted year is needed to reconcile it.
evidence: CASI 70 Years of the PLA Air Force original report (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Number of coded U.S. visits in each direction
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 323. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The table presents PLAAF commander visits to the U.S. and U.S. Air Force commander visits to China as different series.
rows.finding: The underlying table dates three U.S. trips in the outward column and six trips in the inward U.S. line. This reproduces the difference in the published register. It is bounded by the table’s coding, offices and stated years.
evidence: CASI 70 Years of the PLA Air Force original report (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Regional pattern of political commissar visits in the register
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 324. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The diplomatic chapter shows seven visits to five European countries by political commissars.
rows.finding: Counting the dates on the five European country lines in Table 7-2 gives seven, three of them to Russia. This checks the authors’ table calculation within the printed classification.
evidence: CASI 70 Years of the PLA Air Force original report (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Anachronistic dates in the Xinhua delegation comparison
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 327. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The chapter attaches a 1993 source to exchange totals that it describes in a 1993–2003 window. Related printed notes 1787 on PDF p. 467.
rows.finding: The cited vintage and the narrative’s interval are internally incompatible as written. The original dated dispatch is needed to decide whether 1993 or the ten-year range should be corrected.
evidence: CASI 70 Years of the PLA Air Force original report (GovInfo PDF)

rows.source: Launch of the defence ministry’s public-facing website
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 336. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The book cites the U.S. annual report for creation of the ministry’s website in 2009. Related printed notes 1845 on PDF p. 469.
rows.finding: The U.S. report records the 2009 launch. The Chinese defence ministry also dates the public launch to August 2009. This verifies the historical launch and confirms the attribution.
evidence: Defense Department 2010 annual report to Congress
Ministry of National Defense website launch history

The original English republication was unavailable for verbatim comparison.

rows.source: Publication attribution and edition
rows.usage: Supplied PDF cover and imprint, PDF pp. 1–2. Bibliographic comparison.
rows.finding: The supplied PDF front matter names Peter Wood, Alex Stone, Taylor A. Lee and identifies China Aerospace Studies Institute as publisher. Edition or release date is recorded as March 1, 2021.

rows.source: Substantive argument and evidentiary scope
rows.usage: Supplied PDF pp. 7–8. Extracted argument in paraphrase.
rows.finding: Wood, Stone and Lee argue that analysts should assess space institutions and ground infrastructure alongside launch and satellite activity. The opening separates planned commitments from evidence of implementation. A public announcement or agreement establishes a declared relationship at a point in time. This reading establishes the scope of the authors’ argument. Its interpretation and broader empirical inferences need case-specific primary evidence.

rows.source: State Council Information Office, China’s Space Activities in 2016
rows.usage: PDF p. 8 and note 5 on p. 88. Compare sections III and IV of the white paper.
rows.finding: The white paper makes infrastructure a planning priority and distinguishes broad civil space functions in its English rendering. The source supports the report’s documentary attribution. It cannot establish that the proposed infrastructure had entered service on the publication date.
evidence: State Council Information Office, China’s Space Activities in 2016

rows.source: 2020 launch goal compared with reported result
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 10. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper cites 40 launches as a goal for 2020. Related printed notes 1 on PDF p. 88.
rows.finding: The later CASC activity review counts 39 launches by China in 2020 and 89 spacecraft. That is a comparison between a planning goal and the publisher’s realized count. The number of spacecraft is a separate measure.
evidence: CASC annual activity review for 2020, issued in 2021

rows.source: Milestone horizon attributed to a Chinese space planner
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 10. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report cites a three-period strategic timeline from a Chinese planner. Related printed notes 2 on PDF p. 88.
rows.finding: The space white papers provide recognized five-year planning and reporting windows, with selected longer-range ambitions. They do not establish the exact three-date roadmap as a formal state instrument. The cited original remarks and their institutional status are needed.
evidence: State Council archive of the 2016 space white paper
Full text of the 2021 space white paper, issued January 2022

rows.source: Civil space infrastructure plan’s dates and issuers
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The civil space infrastructure plan was issued jointly for the 2015–2025 period. Related printed notes 3 on PDF p. 88.
rows.finding: The official entry identifies Development and Reform, Finance and the defence industry administration as issuing bodies. The title confirms the horizon and the record shows an October 2015 notice. Distinguish the document number from the date.
evidence: Joint civil space infrastructure plan issuance, NDRC register

rows.source: Beidou milestone in the dated space-planning table
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The table lists global Beidou completion as an ambition toward 2020.
rows.finding: The later white paper reports completion and operation of BeiDou-3. This supplies outcome evidence at programme level. It does not support treating earlier constellation-size projections as implemented counts.
evidence: Full text of the 2021 space white paper, issued January 2022

rows.source: Mars mission launch as distinct from landing
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The table lists launching Tianwen-1 as a milestone.
rows.finding: The published annual review places the mission in the 2020 activity cycle and expects arrival the following year. The subsequent white paper records orbit and landing after flight. Separate the launch milestone from the later scientific operations.
evidence: CASC annual activity review for 2020, issued in 2021
Full text of the 2021 space white paper, issued January 2022

rows.source: Civil infrastructure plan’s service categories
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The plan prioritizes remote sensing, communications and broadcasting, and navigation and positioning. Related printed notes 3 on PDF p. 88.
rows.finding: The opening definition and service headings list the three fields and encompass both space- and ground-based components. This supports the category structure independently of the study’s inventory of sites.
evidence: Civil space infrastructure planning document for 2015–2025

rows.source: Role of market mechanisms in the civil space infrastructure plan
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper situates development in a national plan with provision for non-government investment. Related printed notes 3 on PDF p. 88.

rows.source: State Council Information Office, China’s Space Activities in 2016
rows.usage: PDF p. 93, note 36 and the linked short references. Compare white paper section I.

This supports the study’s identification of those themes in official messaging. The document alone cannot measure their frequency across the whole sample or explain how foreign audiences received them.
