rows.source: Priority selection in the first space white paper
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The 2000 white paper describes concentrating resources on a limited set of nationally significant projects. Related printed notes 37 on PDF p. 93.
rows.finding: The archived English text uses limited selection as a development principle and links it to focused breakthroughs. The wording concerns project prioritization and does not establish that the broader programme was limited to few activities.
evidence: November 2000 State Council Information Office white paper, archived reproduction

rows.source: 2006 white paper’s comprehensive development language
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The 2006 white paper explicitly emphasizes coordinated development across different space activities. Related printed notes 38 on PDF p. 93.
rows.finding: The original identifies comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development and calls for overall planning across science, application and technology. Its stated policy can be compared directly with the 2000 text without assuming a complete policy reversal.
evidence: CNSA English archive of the 2006 space white paper

rows.source: Technological breakthroughs in the 2011 space white paper
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The 2011 document emphasizes key technology breakthroughs and resource integration. Related printed notes 39 on PDF p. 93.
rows.finding: The innovation and policy sections confirm the combined emphasis. The current State Council page has a 2014 archive path but the white paper itself is dated December 2011. Cite the document year.
evidence: State Council archive of the 2011 space white paper

rows.source: Legal status of the 2010 U.S. policy at the time of the study
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study says the 2010 National Space Policy remained the operative policy baseline. Related printed notes 127 on PDF p. 96.
rows.finding: The signed 2017 directive expressly amends the 2010 policy, so it was already modified during the study’s period. A new policy was issued December 9, 2020. Retain the original statement as dated and distinguish the amendments from the later replacement.

rows.source: Public and classified documents in the 2018 U.S. space strategy release
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors use the public March 2018 fact sheet to discuss the U.S. space strategy. Related printed notes 132 on PDF p. 97.
rows.finding: The archived March 23 release provides public priorities and four pillars. It supports analysis of the public framing. The fact sheet alone supplies no basis for claiming that each priority corresponds directly to wording in a classified annex.
evidence: White House fact sheet on the March 2018 National Space Strategy

rows.source: Unrelated citation attached to the 2017 Moon and Mars directive
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper describes a new U.S. direction to return people to the Moon and pursue later missions to Mars. Related printed notes 133 on PDF p. 97.
rows.finding: The December 11, 2017 signed memorandum confirms the sequence. Note 133 indexes a presentation on commercial maritime data rather than this directive. Note 134 is closer in subject. Use the signed directive for this sentence.

rows.source: Prudence clause on use of space resources
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 49. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The 2016 white paper describes space resource development and use as prudent. Related printed notes 319 on PDF p. 103.

rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 65. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The international code was proposed as a voluntary space conduct instrument. Related printed notes 467, 469 on PDF p. 108.
rows.finding: Section 1.4 of the March 2014 draft makes subscription voluntary and specifies that the code would be nonbinding. These provisions support the characterization and distinguish the document from a treaty.
evidence: European External Action Service draft international space code, March 31, 2014

rows.source: Transparency and confidence building in the EU draft code
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 65. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The draft uses information and notification measures to support confidence in space activities. Related printed notes 469 on PDF p. 108.
rows.finding: Section 1.3 states the transparency purpose and later provisions specify exchange and notification arrangements. This confirms the function of the draft. The proposal’s text does not establish how states would have implemented it.
evidence: European External Action Service draft international space code, March 31, 2014

rows.source: Russian and Chinese objections to draft code information rules
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 66. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study attributes specific objections about information disclosure to Russia and China. Related printed notes 472 on PDF p. 108.

evidence: European External Action Service draft international space code, March 31, 2014

paper_memo.memo_title: The People’s Liberation Army’s Academic Institutions

sections.heading: Context and core argument
sections.body: Allen and Chen use a bounded inventory to describe mergers, changes in reporting relationships and institutional closures. Their 37 PLA schools include 34 officer and three NCO institutions. Counts depend on which services, subordinate schools and other forces are in scope.

sections.heading: How to read the evidence
sections.body: Read the post-reform roster as a dated administrative snapshot. Track mergers and predecessor names to avoid counting the same institution twice.

sections.heading: Citation and claim checks
sections.body: **Ministry of National Defense briefing on the 2017 military school roster.** PDF pp. 5–6, number of institutions. Compared with the Ministry briefing preserved by a provincial government. The official briefing reports 43 schools across the PLA and People’s Armed Police, including six PAP institutions. Its remaining 37 are consistent with the paper’s PLA-only total. The official grouping of two directly subordinate and 35 service schools uses a different classification from the authors’ 34 officer and three NCO schools. Those subcategories require an institution-by-institution match.

rows.source: Substantive argument and evidentiary scope
rows.usage: Supplied PDF pp. 7–8. Extracted argument in paraphrase.
rows.finding: Corbett frames runway recovery as an institutional resilience problem and draws on historical examples and public reporting. An exercise narrative provides evidence of what was reported about a bounded event. General conclusions about recovery under conflict conditions need independent validation with comparable conditions and outcomes. This reading establishes the scope of the authors’ argument. rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 8. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper draws on both earlier English-language analysis and Chinese primary-source reports.

rows.finding: The introduction highlights the source limitation and the research discussion on p. 11 separately says that recorded timings are taken from reports and are not a comprehensive performance measure. The two passages agree on the limitation; they support no claim about actual performance.

rows.source: Absence of public reporting on surprise drills as a sampling limit
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study found few sources describing unannounced drills in the material it surveyed.
rows.finding: The method discussion and selected endnotes identify a public-source sample. The study supplies no comprehensive exercise calendar. The evidence supports a statement about what the author observed, with the frequency across real training left open.

rows.source: Reported times cannot establish a general capability distribution
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper presents time observations reported by sources rather than a measured aggregate.
rows.finding: The same section explicitly restricts the meaning of the figures and the introduction identifies the evidence as selected public reports. This confirms why the case measurements cannot serve as a general performance estimate. No timing details are reproduced here.

rows.source: Publication attribution and edition
rows.usage: Supplied PDF cover and imprint, PDF pp. 1–2. Bibliographic comparison.
rows.finding: The supplied PDF front matter names Kevin Pollpeter, Elizabeth Barrett, Jeffrey Edmonds, Amanda Kerrigan, Andrew Taffer and identifies China Aerospace Studies Institute as publisher. Edition or release date is recorded as May 8, 2023.
evidence: China-Russia Space Cooperation: The Strategic, Military, Diplomatic, and Economic Implications of a Growing Relationship

rows.source: Substantive argument and evidentiary scope
rows.usage: Supplied PDF pp. 4–5, 21. Extracted argument in paraphrase.
rows.finding: The authors treat space cooperation as a set of diplomatic, economic and institutional relationships. Their framing distinguishes a strategic partnership from a formal alliance. Agreements, roadmaps and completed projects are different milestones, and an announced collaboration can evolve after a study closes. This reading establishes the scope of the authors’ argument. Its interpretation and broader empirical inferences need case-specific primary evidence.
evidence: China-Russia Space Cooperation: The Strategic, Military, Diplomatic, and Economic Implications of a Growing Relationship

rows.source: CNSA, China and Russia sign the ILRS cooperation memorandum
rows.usage: PDF p. 21 and pp. 62–63, notes 76, 98 and 99. Note 76 has additional sources.
rows.finding: The issuing agency confirms that CNSA and Roscosmos signed the intergovernmental memorandum on March 9, 2021. It describes joint planning and envisaged cooperation. This confirms the reported signing and purpose. Delivery and any broader claim about alliance commitments need distinct evidence.
evidence: CNSA, China and Russia sign the ILRS cooperation memorandum

rows.source: Date of the China–Russia new-era strategic partnership
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The bilateral relationship was upgraded using new-era strategic-partnership language in 2019.
rows.finding: SCIO records the June 2019 Moscow joint statement and its full designation. This confirms the relationship label, which is diplomatic terminology rather than a mutual-defence obligation.
evidence: SCIO chronology and June 2019 China–Russia statement date

rows.source: 1996 strategic partnership milestone
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report dates the strategic partnership to the 1990s, before the 2019 upgrade. Related printed notes 4 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The Foreign Ministry chronology distinguishes the 1994 constructive partnership and 1996 strategic partnership. The SCIO timeline records the later comprehensive and new-era milestones. These are separate changes in official designation.
evidence: Ministry of Foreign Affairs chronology of China–Russia diplomatic relations
SCIO chronology and June 2019 China–Russia statement date

rows.source: China and Russia as founding SCO members
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. China and Russia were among the states that established the SCO in 2001. Related printed notes 7 on PDF p. 56.
rows.finding: The 2019 official white paper lists six founding states and dates establishment to June 2001. This confirms their founding role within a multilateral organization.
evidence: SCIO 2019 defence white paper, SCO section

rows.source: Scope of the no-restricted-areas rhetoric
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 15. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The cited remarks portray bilateral cooperation as open-ended. Related printed notes 21 on PDF p. 58.
rows.finding: The February 2022 joint declaration contains similar wording on friendship and areas of cooperation. This establishes a later joint formulation. It does not verify the earlier remarks’ exact wording or imply an enforceable mutual-defence guarantee.

rows.source: Signature and entry into force of the 1992 peaceful space agreement
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 19. Extracted claim in paraphrase. China and Russia concluded a bilateral peaceful space cooperation agreement in December 1992. Related printed notes 60 on PDF p. 61.
rows.finding: The foreign ministry treaty record gives signature in Beijing and entry into force on December 18, 1992. The treaty registry establishes the nature of the instrument and the dates. It gives no count of resulting contracts.
evidence: PRC treaty registry entry for December 18, 1992 peaceful space cooperation agreement

rows.source: 93 contracts attributed to the 1992 cooperation framework
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 19. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report attributes 93 contracts to the early intergovernmental space agreement. Related printed notes 60 on PDF p. 61.
rows.finding: The treaty registry confirms the framework and the 2001 communiqué confirms recurring bilateral cooperation. Neither lists 93 space contracts or defines the period and contract types included. The underlying contract register or full institutional history is needed.
evidence: PRC treaty registry entry for December 18, 1992 peaceful space cooperation agreement
Official joint heads-of-state statement referencing the sixth meeting of premiers

rows.source: Distinction between premiers’ meetings and space subcommittee meetings
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 19. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report says the space subcommittee first met in May 2000 under the broader regular-premiers mechanism. Related printed notes 62 on PDF p. 61.
rows.finding: The July 2001 joint statement refers to the sixth regular premiers’ meeting due that September. That establishes the parent mechanism by 2001. It does not date the first meeting of the specialized space subcommittee. The subcommittee minutes are required.
evidence: Official joint heads-of-state statement referencing the sixth meeting of premiers

rows.source: Year of approval of China’s lunar programme
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 21. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The lunar exploration programme was formally approved in January 2004.
rows.finding: The official retrospective confirms January 2004 as approval and beginning of development. The project center’s chronology describes the three-phase programme. The day-level date needs the approval instrument itself.
evidence: CNSA historical account of the Chang’e 5 sample-return mission
CNSA Lunar Exploration Center chronology of lunar programme milestones

rows.source: Chang’e 1 first lunar mission
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 21. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The first Chinese lunar probe launched in 2007 and mapped the Moon. Related printed notes 80 on PDF p. 62.
rows.finding: The 2011 white paper reports launch on October 24, 2007 and acquisition of a complete lunar map. The project center separately situates the mission in the orbital science phase. This supports the mission milestone.
evidence: State Council archive of the 2011 space white paper
CNSA Lunar Exploration Center chronology of lunar programme milestones

rows.source: Chang’e 2 transition from lunar mapping to an asteroid flyby
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 21. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The mission moved from lunar mapping to later deep-space science activity. Related printed notes 81 on PDF p. 63.
rows.finding: The project center dates the launch to October 1, 2010 and identifies the subsequent close encounter with Toutatis. These are distinct phases of the same mission.
evidence: CNSA Lunar Exploration Center chronology of lunar programme milestones

rows.source: Chang’e 3 landing and Yutu rover
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 22. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The mission landed in 2013 and delivered Yutu to the Moon. Related printed notes 82 on PDF p. 63.
rows.finding: The national project history and space white paper describe the 2013 soft landing and rover exploration. These records establish the milestone without relying on the unrelated British space programme framing of the cited article.
evidence: CNSA Lunar Exploration Center chronology of lunar programme milestones
State Council archive of the 2016 space white paper

rows.source: Chang’e 4 mission launch and far-side landing
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 22. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The mission achieved the first lunar far-side soft landing. Related printed notes 83 on PDF p. 63.
rows.finding: The project center distinguishes launch on December 8, 2018 from landing on January 3, 2019. This establishes the first soft landing on the lunar far side and explains why both years occur in citations.
evidence: CNSA Lunar Exploration Center chronology of lunar programme milestones

rows.source: Chang’e 5 sample return
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 22. Extracted claim in paraphrase. Chang’e 5 collected and brought lunar samples to Earth in 2020. Related printed notes 84 on PDF p. 63.
rows.finding: The agency mission record and January 2022 white paper both report sample return in December 2020. This establishes completion of the sample return phase of the original lunar programme.
evidence: CNSA historical account of the Chang’e 5 sample-return mission
Full text of the 2021 space white paper, issued January 2022

rows.source: Version and date of the lunar research station roadmap
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 23. Extracted claim in paraphrase. A joint roadmap and partnership guide were released in June 2021. Related printed notes 104 on PDF p. 64.
rows.finding: CNSA records publication of roadmap version 1.0 and partner guide version 1.0 on June 16. It anticipates further versions. The publication confirms the joint planning milestone, while projections remain dated.
evidence: CNSA announcement of the June 2021 roadmap and partner guide

rows.source: Partner participation in the lunar research station
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 24. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The programme documents invite participation beyond China and Russia. Related printed notes 105 on PDF p. 64.
rows.finding: The joint statement and roadmap invite interested partners across several project phases. The invitations document intended openness. They provide no list of concluded accession arrangements.
evidence: CNSA announcement of the June 2021 roadmap and partner guide
CNSA and Roscosmos joint statement on lunar research station partnership

rows.source: Chronology of Artemis signatures and the bilateral lunar memorandum
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 25. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The initial Artemis signatures preceded the 2021 lunar research station memorandum. Related printed notes 109 on PDF p. 64.
rows.finding: NASA dates the first eight signatures to October 13, 2020, including the United States. The Chinese agency’s release dates the separate bilateral memorandum March 9, 2021. The event order is documented. Motive and causation remain interpretive.
evidence: NASA record of the original Artemis Accords signatures
CNSA’s March 9 memorandum announcement and description of earlier agreements

rows.source: Artemis Accords’ relationship to existing treaties
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 25. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The accords articulate principles to guide civil activity in support of the Artemis programme. Related printed notes 110, 111 on PDF p. 64.
rows.finding: The signed text describes a political understanding and references the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, rescue, liability and registration instruments. This supports the distinction between Artemis program activity and the broader international treaty framework.

rows.source: U.S. appropriation restrictions and China joining Artemis
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 26. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study links bilateral legal constraints to uncertainty about U.S. participation with China.
rows.finding: The initial 2011 provision limits use of specified NASA and OSTP appropriations for bilateral collaboration absent authorization. The 2020 Accords text describes a political framework. The two documents do not establish universal legal ineligibility. An applicable fiscal-year provision and proposed activity are necessary for that conclusion.
evidence: United States Public Law 112-10, 2011 appropriations, section 1340

rows.source: Original PPWT submission date
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 43. Extracted claim in paraphrase. China and Russia submitted an initial PPWT draft in 2008. Related printed notes 227 on PDF p. 71.
rows.finding: Their joint follow-up identifies CD/1839 and its February 29, 2008 document date. The 2014 plenary record describes it as the earlier submission. This was a draft in the Conference on Disarmament.
evidence: 2009 Chinese–Russian answers referring to original proposal CD/1839
Conference on Disarmament June 10, 2014 plenary record, CD/PV.1319

rows.source: Revised PPWT submission and circulation dates
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 43. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The two states submitted a revised space arms-control proposal in 2014. Related printed notes 229 on PDF p. 72.
rows.finding: The June 10 plenary records the joint submission. The revised instrument CD/1985 is dated June 12. Those dates refer to the introduction and circulated text respectively. The references document a proposal, not a treaty in force.
evidence: Conference on Disarmament June 10, 2014 plenary record, CD/PV.1319
Conference on Disarmament CD/1985, revised treaty proposal

rows.source: Separate earlier Chang’e 7 coordination agreement
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 52. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The appendix lists a separate pre-ILRS cooperation instrument for coordination involving the Chang’e 7 mission. Related printed notes 251 on PDF p. 73.
rows.finding: The March 2021 memorandum announcement identifies an already signed coordination agreement. The 2021 white paper distinguishes that coordination from the lunar station project and from data-centre cooperation. The release does not give the agreement’s signed date in isolation.
evidence: CNSA’s March 9 memorandum announcement and description of earlier agreements
Full text of the 2021 space white paper, issued January 2022

rows.source: Lunar and deep-space data centre agreement in the agreement table
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 52. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The agreement table lists a distinct arrangement for a shared lunar and deep-space data centre. Related printed notes 253 on PDF p. 73.
rows.finding: CNSA names this as a previously signed agreement separate from the Chang’e 7 coordination. The January 2022 white paper records that centre construction was initiated. These accounts do not establish a date of full operation.
evidence: CNSA’s March 9 memorandum announcement and description of earlier agreements
Full text of the 2021 space white paper, issued January 2022

rows.source: Date and topic of the 2008 joint position on financial reform
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 14. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report uses the joint statement to show agreement on reform of international financial institutions. Related printed notes 10 on PDF p. 57.
rows.finding: The original MFA text was issued on 23 May 2008 and gives a common position on international economic and financial governance. Agreement in the communiqué is a public diplomatic finding.
evidence: Original 2008 China–Russia statement on major international issues

rows.source: Exact attribution of the 2019 assessment of strategic alignment
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 15. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report quotes the U.S. intelligence community's statement about the strongest alignment since the mid-1950s. Related printed notes 22 on PDF p. 58.
rows.finding: The signed assessment for the Senate in January 2019 contains the comparison and distinguishes current alignment from the earlier formal relationship.
evidence: Director of National Intelligence’s January 2019 statement for the record

rows.source: Consultation clause in the 2001 friendship treaty
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 15. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study distinguishes bilateral security coordination from a mutual-defence commitment. Related printed notes 23 on PDF p. 58.
rows.finding: Article 9 provides for contacts and consultations when either party sees a threat to peace or its security. The instrument’s text supports the distinction between consultation and an automatic assistance obligation.
evidence: Chinese foreign ministry's text of the 2001 friendship treaty

rows.source: 2018 milestone of 100 billion dollars in bilateral commodity trade
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 15. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper identifies 2018 as a new threshold in bilateral trade. Related printed notes 27 on PDF p. 58.
rows.finding: Chinese official trade material gives the 2018 milestone and identifies the goods-trade basis. The figure combines exports and imports valued in U.S. dollars.
evidence: Ministry of Commerce official Russia country guide
Commerce Ministry press conference on bilateral trade

rows.source: Bilateral trade remained above the threshold in 2020
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 15. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study states that the threshold was exceeded again despite the intervening year’s circumstances. Related printed notes 27 on PDF p. 58.
rows.finding: The Commerce Ministry reports approximately 107.8 billion U.S. dollars for 2020 and a year-on-year decline. This supports the threshold claim without implying that trade grew in both years.
evidence: Commerce Ministry press conference on bilateral trade

rows.source: Institutional signatories of the 2018 academies agreement
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 16. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study cites a CAS agreement with the Russian Academy of Sciences as part of the civil science chronology. Related printed notes 34 on PDF p. 59.
rows.finding: The Chinese academy’s signing account identifies the two science academies and dates the institutional agreement. Subsequent projects are separately documented.
evidence: Chinese Academy of Sciences signing account with the Russian academy

rows.source: Scientific innovation language in the 2019 joint statement
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 16. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report quotes enhanced bilateral scientific and technological collaboration as an expressly stated diplomatic aim. Related printed notes 35 on PDF p. 59.
rows.finding: The published bilateral text gives priority to deeper innovation cooperation. It provides evidence for the agreed wording and policy status.
evidence: 2019 bilateral partnership statement published by a Chinese embassy

rows.source: Innovation Dialogue institutionalisation across successive meetings
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 16. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper describes the 2016 agreement to develop a dialogue that subsequently convened repeatedly. Related printed notes 36, 37 on PDF p. 59.
rows.finding: MOST’s accounts date the second meeting to 2018 and third to 2019. They confirm institutionalisation and recurrence, while the 2016 description concerns the initial agreement.
evidence: MOST official second China–Russia Innovation Dialogue release
MOST official third China–Russia Innovation Dialogue release

rows.source: Dating the China–Russia atmospheric optics centre
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 16. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study places establishment of the joint centre in Anhui in 2019. Related printed notes 39 on PDF p. 59.
rows.finding: The signatory institute’s 2019 report records creation of the collaborative centre and the local host. The later Hefei academy account independently identifies the centre’s continuing work.
evidence: CAS signing institution’s 2019 account of atmospheric optics collaboration
Hefei institute joint centre symposium report

rows.source: Opening date of the bilateral innovation year
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 16. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper dates the launch of the China–Russia science and technology innovation year to August 2020. Related printed notes 40 on PDF p. 59.
rows.finding: The Ministry of Science and Technology records the opening ceremony on 26 August 2020 and gives the two-year 2020–2021 programme scope.
evidence: MOST original China–Russia science and technology year opening announcement

rows.source: Investment ranking uses direct investment counterpart positions
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 17. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study uses IMF bilateral direct investment data for a 2009–2019 ranking. Related printed notes 51 on PDF p. 60.
rows.finding: The IMF series measures positions by immediate counterpart economy. Reproducing the ranks needs the period-specific download, reporter direction, geography coding and missing-data conventions. The statistic cannot by itself capture ultimate ownership.
evidence: IMF investment counterpart economy methodological guidance

rows.source: Status of the 2014 Crimea annexation in the UN record
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 14. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report uses Crimea as a historical turning point for Russian relations with Western governments. Related printed notes 13 on PDF p. 57.
rows.finding: The UN General Assembly’s March 2014 resolution affirms Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and treats the referendum as having no validity for altering Crimea’s status. It establishes the contemporary UN response, while the causal assessment is the authors’.
evidence: UN General Assembly resolution 68/262 on the territorial integrity of Ukraine

rows.source: Publication decade of the cited 2016 Chinese space white paper
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 19. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The related note identifies the 2016 white paper but gives a 2006 release date. Related printed notes 65 on PDF p. 61.
rows.finding: The official CNSA version is the 2016 white paper published on 27 December 2016. The publication year in the citation should match the edition named in the title.

rows.source: Signing year versus effective period of the 2018–2022 space cooperation outline
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 20. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The main text describes a 2018–2022 programme, and the appendix records 2018 as the year signed. Related printed notes 72, 258 on PDF p. 62, 74.
rows.finding: CNSA announced the signing in November 2017. The programme starts in 2018, so the appendix’s year-signed column should carry 2017 for this instrument.
evidence: CNSA announcement of the five-year outline

rows.source: 2011 interview as evidence for a later cooperation outline
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 20. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The text places Yin Liming’s remarks in its discussion of the 2018–2022 outline. Related printed notes 74 on PDF p. 62.
rows.finding: The interview cited in note 74 is dated August 2011, several years before the November 2017 signing. It can be cited for the earlier context and requires separate evidence for reaction to the later programme.
evidence: China Daily contemporary interview on 2011 bilateral cooperation
CNSA announcement of the five-year outline

rows.source: Tianhe core module launch chronology
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report starts its construction chronology with the April 2021 core-module launch. Related printed notes 120 on PDF p. 65.
rows.finding: CMSA’s mission page dates the Tianhe launch to 29 April 2021. The date concerns the core-module mission.

rows.source: Actual completion of the station’s construction phase
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report relays a planned 2022 completion year for construction of the Chinese station. Related printed notes 120 on PDF p. 65.
rows.finding: CMSA subsequently describes completion of the basic station configuration in 2022. Treat the report’s wording as a forecast that later agency milestones corroborate at the year level.
evidence: CMSA Shenzhou-17 retrospective and station programme

rows.source: Retirement horizon for the ISS discussed in the 2023 study
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The Russian cooperation study considers a 2025 ISS retirement in its station-access discussion. Related printed notes 122 on PDF p. 65.
rows.finding: The U.S. statutory continuation horizon is 2030. The paper’s 2025 scenario should be dated explicitly when used to discuss later station availability.
evidence: U.S. Code section 18351 on ISS continuation

rows.source: Yinghuo-1 as a passenger instrument mission
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes China's planned Mars orbiter as launched on the Russian Phobos-Grunt mission. Related printed notes 132 on PDF p. 65.
rows.finding: NASA's mission history identifies Yinghuo-1 as a separate Chinese spacecraft carried with Phobos-Grunt, and places both on the November 2011 launch. It never reached Mars orbit.

rows.source: Phobos-Grunt’s Earth-orbit outcome and re-entry
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper dates the failed mission’s atmospheric re-entry to 15 January 2012. Related printed notes 133, 134 on PDF p. 66.
rows.finding: NASA’s mission chronology records the unsuccessful departure from Earth orbit and lists 15 January 2012 for re-entry. This establishes outcome and timing independently of claims about the failure cause.

rows.source: Tianwen-2 actual launch versus the early 2024 forecast
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 28. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper relays an early launch expectation for the mission to Kamo’oalewa.
rows.finding: CNSA reports that Tianwen-2 launched on 29 May 2025. The earlier date was a forecast and the actual launch provides a dated update. Sampling results remain a separate milestone.
evidence: CNSA report of the Tianwen-2 launch

rows.source: Date of the Sino-Russian space debris agreement
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 35. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper gives 11 November 2018 as the signing date for the CNSA and Roscosmos debris agreement. Related printed notes 181, 182 on PDF p. 68, 69.
rows.finding: CNSA’s 10 November announcement dates the signing itself to 7 November 2018. The agency publicised the agreement three days after signature.
evidence: CNSA signing announcement for debris monitoring agreement

rows.source: Status of the proposed debris information exchange arrangement
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 35. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study refers to a joint information-exchange system as an intended output of the debris agreement. Related printed notes 181 on PDF p. 68.
rows.finding: CNSA confirms signature and describes intended cooperation. The full instrument and implementation reports are needed to establish the terms and whether the specific exchange became operational.
evidence: CNSA signing announcement for debris monitoring agreement

rows.source: Civil navigation joint statement and later treaty status
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 38. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes the 2015 joint statement as a precursor to intergovernmental cooperation. Related printed notes 196 on PDF p. 69.
rows.finding: The 2019 administration account confirms the earlier compatibility statement as a separate step and distinguishes it from the later peace-use instrument signed in November 2018.
evidence: CNSA notice on approval of the navigation agreement

rows.source: Signature and approval milestones for peaceful-use navigation agreement
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 39. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report records the signature of a bilateral peaceful-use agreement in November 2018. Related printed notes 202, 203 on PDF p. 70.
rows.finding: CNSA identifies 7 November 2018 as the signature date. Its August 2019 release records Russian presidential approval and still conditions entry into force on completion of diplomatic procedures.
evidence: CNSA notice on approval of the navigation agreement

rows.source: Document status of the 2021–2025 navigation roadmap
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 39. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes the October 2020 committee meeting as discussing the roadmap. Related printed notes 205 on PDF p. 70.
rows.finding: The published accounts establish that a roadmap was considered. A signed copy or official entry list is needed to distinguish consideration, approval, and execution of the instrument.

rows.source: 2018 letter of intent has a later Russian citation
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 53. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The appendix gives the 2018 lunar and deep-space letter of intent an accompanying Russian citation naming the International Lunar Research Station memorandum. Related printed notes 260, 261 on PDF p. 74.
rows.finding: CNSA dates the intergovernmental research-station memorandum to March 2021. The 2021 instrument should have its own citation, leaving the Russian text of the 2018 letter as a specific gap.
evidence: CNSA notice of bilateral lunar research station memorandum
CNSA official 2021 space white paper English text

rows.source: Scope of the agreement chronology and the 1994 entry
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 54. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The table lists a 1994 item alongside its explicitly described 2009–2021 agreement set. Related printed notes 271, 272 on PDF p. 74, 75.
rows.finding: The included line predates the stated scope. Official later cooperation statements confirm a longer bilateral history but the original 1994 instrument is needed to establish its title and how it relates to the 1992 agreement.

sections.heading: Context and core argument
sections.body: The authors treat space cooperation as a set of diplomatic, economic and institutional relationships. Their framing distinguishes a strategic partnership from a formal alliance. Agreements, roadmaps and completed projects are different milestones, and an announced collaboration can evolve after a study closes.

sections.heading: How to read the evidence
sections.body: Date the evidence to each agreement or public announcement. Use civil space milestones as evidence of declared joint intent and examine delivery separately.

sections.heading: Citation and claim checks
sections.body: **CNSA, China and Russia sign the ILRS cooperation memorandum.** PDF p. 21 and pp. 62–63, notes 76, 98 and 99. Note 76 has additional sources. The issuing agency confirms that CNSA and Roscosmos signed the intergovernmental memorandum on March 9, 2021. It describes joint planning and envisaged cooperation. This confirms the reported signing and purpose. Delivery and any broader claim about alliance commitments need distinct evidence.

rows.source: Publication attribution and edition
rows.usage: Supplied PDF cover and imprint, PDF pp. 1–2. Bibliographic comparison.
rows.finding: The supplied PDF front matter names Geoffrey Chambers (analytics) and identifies China Aerospace Studies Institute as publisher. Edition or release date is recorded as December 5, 2022.

rows.source: Substantive argument and evidentiary scope
rows.usage: Supplied PDF pp. 10–14. Extracted argument in paraphrase.
rows.finding: The BluePath study applies bibliometric methods to a selected research corpus. It adapts citation metrics within that specific corpus. Publication volume and citation influence respond to selection, coverage and naming conventions, so their interpretation depends on the sample boundary and reproducibility of the search. This reading establishes the scope of the authors’ argument. Its interpretation and broader empirical inferences need case-specific primary evidence.

rows.source: Method uses a published 2012 baseline and later bibliometrics
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors construct their analytical baseline from a 2012 book and compare it to later publication data.
rows.finding: The methodology and the book’s bibliographic imprint transcribed in the supplied report identify the 2012 authors and edition. The limitations section describes why the qualitative baseline and later data should not be expected to match exactly.

rows.source: Publication observation window
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The quantitative literature search ends December 31, 2020 and starts in 2012.
rows.finding: The method specifies a bounded 2012–2020 document window and the growth definition uses those same years. It does not include later publications even if the report was issued later.

rows.source: Meaning of the 300 million source corpus figure
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The overall indexed databases represent more than 300 million documents before the study’s query.
rows.finding: The immediate sentence describes the source universe, not the final query output. The analytical stages work from a smaller corpus. Source database snapshots and the retrieval log are needed to replicate the stated universe at the acquisition date.

rows.source: Retention of broader research clusters
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The researchers retain some broader clusters to reduce the risk of omission.
rows.finding: The methods describe keeping clusters with broader application potential. The next measurement section defines topical relevance as a share of documents, and the limitations discuss classification error. This is a deliberate recall choice with uncertain precision.

rows.source: Status of the seventh quantitative subsection
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The seventh quantitative subsection covers a direction not matched to the 2012 book’s framework.
rows.finding: The organization statement on p. 15 and table of contents identify seven subsections and distinguish the separately added seventh. The study’s seventh theme should not be attributed to the 2012 authors.

rows.source: Patents play a supplementary role in the study
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report uses patent data to supplement bibliometric results where articles are sparse.
rows.finding: The methodology states that articles and patents serve different coverage functions. The later indicator definitions keep the units separate. Patent counts support an observation about public filings and do not by themselves show transfer to use.

rows.source: Regression slope units in the growth measure
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study’s growth indicator is fitted change in publications per year.
rows.finding: The definition and worked example state that a slope of 7.43 means about 7.43 additional documents per year. It is neither a percentage nor the number of documents published in every calendar year.

rows.source: Topical relevance indicator is a document share
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The relevance indicator applies a title-or-abstract keyword rule to each cluster.
rows.finding: The definition specifies its numerator and denominator. The later limitations acknowledge the mismatch between quantitative clusters and the report’s qualitative baseline. The metric can compare focus within the corpus, but cannot independently verify technical progress.

rows.source: Different units for the 31 baseline categories and 64 research clusters
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 14. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study contrasts a qualitative set of topics with 64 publication clusters.
rows.finding: The limits section explicitly warns that a perfect match is unrealistic. Compare the qualitative summary on p. 4 with the seven-subsection organization on p. 15. The two totals describe different units and do not imply 33 new technologies.

rows.source: Evidentiary limits of the open-source research landscape comparison
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 14. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors define their result as a review based on publications and other open information.
rows.finding: The publisher’s methodology explicitly sets that scope. Its data describe observable publication and patent activity, with the coverage limits recorded by the authors.
evidence: CASI publication and explanation of research methodology

rows.source: Treatment of analyst judgement in thematic cluster mapping
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 14. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report describes manual matching of the literature to its baseline as a judgement step.
rows.finding: The methodology notes substantive expertise limitations and possible mapping error. Replication would require row-level assignments and independent coding of the same document sample.
evidence: CASI publication and explanation of research methodology

rows.source: AHP attribution and methodological editions
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 21. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper traces its interpretation of hierarchical decision analysis to Saaty.
rows.finding: Saaty’s methods papers confirm the use of hierarchies and pairwise judgement. They directly distinguish the 1980 AHP book from the 1982 Decision Making for Leaders volume mentioned in the report.
evidence: Saaty’s original methods paper on analytic hierarchy

rows.source: Unreported decision panel composition
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 22. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper flags that the primary scoring study provides limited respondent detail.
rows.finding: The report reproduces selected scoring results, and Saaty's source explains how comparisons enter the method. The respondent roster and elicitation instrument are needed for independent replication of the judgement inputs.
evidence: CASI publication and explanation of research methodology
Saaty’s original methods paper on analytic hierarchy

rows.source: Limits of patent counts as evidence of commercial performance
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 27. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report treats patent records as a possible indicator of development activity.
rows.finding: The OECD manual recognises patent data as an innovation indicator while explaining differences in propensity, jurisdiction and economic value. Evidence of commercial application requires a separate measure.

rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 7. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper distinguishes state, provincial or ministerial, municipal and institution-level laboratories. Related printed notes 1 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: The documents define national innovation facilities and identify provincial co-sponsorship within a national programme. The report’s Figure 1 uses tiers as an analytical description. Provincial partnership alone does not determine the institutional classification of a specific lab.
evidence: MOST, Finance Ministry and NDRC integration scheme for national research bases
MOST and Finance Ministry opinion on development of State Key Laboratories

rows.source: Which laboratory count the estimated 700 covers
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 9. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper associates roughly 700 labs with the State Key Laboratory system and its subtypes.
rows.finding: The June 2018 opinion uses approximately 700 for a 2020 planning target. NBS reports 522 State Key Laboratories in operation at year-end 2020. The scope and inclusion basis differ from the study’s broader categories. Treat the target and inventory as distinct until subtype definitions are reconciled.
evidence: Science and Technology Daily contemporary summary of the 2018 laboratory targets

rows.source: State Key Laboratory count was a policy target
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 10. Extracted claim in paraphrase. MOST and the Finance Ministry aimed for roughly 700 State Key Laboratories by 2020. Related printed notes 9 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: The opinion sets a target of around 700 with differentiated targets for major categories. It is a planning benchmark. The issuance does not report that all of them were in operation.
evidence: MOST and Finance Ministry opinion on development of State Key Laboratories
Science and Technology Daily contemporary summary of the 2018 laboratory targets

rows.source: Measurement of the reported State Key Laboratory shortfall
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 10. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report estimates a shortfall of about 150, concentrated among business-sector labs. Related printed notes 10, 11 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: The 2020 official headline count of 522 is 178 below a nominal target of 700. Figure 3 uses a different date and subtype estimates. The comparison verifies an overall gap at the headline level but not the allocation of the gap among subtypes.
evidence: Science and Technology Daily contemporary summary of the 2018 laboratory targets
China Association for Science and Technology 2020–2021 discipline development report

rows.source: Business-sector laboratory estimate in the report’s intermediate census
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 10. Extracted claim in paraphrase. Figure 3 reports an estimate of 174 business-sector labs against a target of 270. Related printed notes 11 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: The policy specifies the category and target. The NBS summary reports an aggregate and does not provide the report’s business-sector count. CAST’s later report also gives 174 as under construction or operating at year-end 2020, explicitly including multiple approval cohorts. This corroborates the magnitude while leaving the May observation date and operating-only count open.
evidence: Science and Technology Daily contemporary summary of the 2018 laboratory targets
China Association for Science and Technology 2020–2021 discipline development report

rows.source: Reported early approval split by institutional host
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The historical approval count is presented as 35 labs in universities and 20 in research institutes. Related printed notes 17 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: The subtotals reconcile to 55. The later directives distinguish types of host organizations and different laboratory categories. They do not verify the historical approval census attributed to Li Zhongjie. The original approvals or the cited pages are needed.
evidence: MOST, Finance Ministry and NDRC integration scheme for national research bases
MOST and Finance Ministry opinion on development of State Key Laboratories

rows.source: Distinction between the publicly cited list and analytical sample
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors start from a 60-entry list and retain 56 after exclusions. Related printed notes 18 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: The report’s methods on p. 14 repeat the screening. The public restructuring notice shows why designations can change, but does not supply the cited archived list. The identities of the four exclusions and the original list are needed for full reproducibility.
evidence: MOST, Finance Ministry and NDRC integration scheme for national research bases

rows.source: Meaning of the 45 similarly named laboratories
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The authors identified 45 additional labs using the same or a similar designation without establishing the same formal status.
rows.finding: The 2017 and 2018 rules distinguish several formal categories. The extra 45 in the report refer to label usage and do not extend the confirmed sample. A dated approval notice for each lab would establish its administrative category.
evidence: MOST, Finance Ministry and NDRC integration scheme for national research bases
Five authorities’ June 2018 resource-sharing management rules

rows.source: Three categories of national innovation bases in the 2017 scheme
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The scheme distinguishes research, innovation and transfer, and infrastructure or resource support. Related printed notes 20 on PDF p. 25.
rows.finding: The three categories are explicitly enumerated in the signed scheme. The grouping is functional. It does not by itself determine the rank, status or output of each site.
evidence: MOST, Finance Ministry and NDRC integration scheme for national research bases

rows.source: June 2018 research-resource sharing instrument
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 13. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The management rules promote reciprocal sharing among civilian and defence research institutions. Related printed notes 21 on PDF p. 25.
rows.finding: The signed instrument confirms the multi-agency issuance and broad reciprocal sharing policy. It maintains security controls. The directive establishes obligations and authorized scope, while participation by individual institutions remains a separate question.
evidence: Five authorities’ June 2018 resource-sharing management rules

rows.source: Two laboratory tiers in the 2021 leadership address
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 9. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The study treats national laboratories and state key laboratories as different levels of the system. Related printed notes 4 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: Xi's May 2021 address calls for a national laboratory system led by national labs and for reorganising the state key labs. The national plan also assigns those initiatives separate roles.

rows.source: Sector coverage of the 700-lab policy target
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 10. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper counts company-based labs within the same planning benchmark as other state key labs. Related printed notes 9 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: The 2018 policy defines the overall total across disciplinary, enterprise, and joint ministry–province state key laboratories. Its enterprise programme has its own development provisions within that total.
evidence: MOST and Finance Ministry state key laboratory development policy

rows.source: Competing historical defence laboratory totals
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 11. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The report gives 55 and 60 as differing historical cited counts for the defence laboratory category. Related printed notes 17, 18 on PDF p. 24.
rows.finding: The supplied report identifies different underlying materials, including a now-unavailable official roster. A dated roster and contemporary classification rules remain needed to resolve the difference in coverage.
evidence: CASI report and research notes on the state laboratory system (BluePath Labs PDF)

rows.source: Placement of state laboratories in the science and engineering category
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper's table places national labs and state key labs under science and engineering research. Related printed notes 20 on PDF p. 25.
rows.finding: The plan lists both alongside scientific research centres in its science and engineering category. The scheme also assigns separate mandates to transfer and research-service institutions.
evidence: Three agencies' national innovation base consolidation plan

rows.source: Different support instruments for research bases and transfer centres
rows.usage: Supplied PDF p. 12. Extracted claim in paraphrase. The paper distinguishes exploratory research from transfer and infrastructure functions in the new system. Related printed notes 20 on PDF p. 25.
rows.finding: The underlying plan differentiates mandates and gives stable fiscal support priority for research and support infrastructure, while applying market guidance, assessments and potential ex-post subsidies to technology transfer bases.
evidence: Three agencies' national innovation base consolidation plan

paper_memo.memo_title: The PRC State & Defense Laboratory System: An Overview

sections.heading: Context and core argument
sections.body: Stone and Ma distinguish laboratory categories and present the two systems in the context of national innovation policy. A policy calling for reorganization establishes an official priority. Directory entries and sponsorship records can help trace implementation, but their coverage and category boundaries vary by date.

sections.heading: How to read the evidence
sections.body: Keep national laboratories, national key laboratories and defense research designations separate when reconciling successive directories.

sections.heading: Citation and claim checks
sections.body: **National Development and Reform Commission, Fourteenth Plan explanation of the laboratory system.** PDF p. 6 and endnote 2 on p. 24. The NDRC explanation is supplementary to the cited plan. The Planning Department distinguishes national laboratories from State Key Laboratories and describes consolidation, adjustment and reregistration. This confirms the published reorganization priority and the distinction between categories. It supplies no completed census of either system.

sections.heading: Coverage and remaining gaps
sections.body:
All 32 detected numbered positions link to an index row. New source references were recorded for 6 positions. Cited-passage or related evidence comparisons are recorded for 6 positions.

Visual inspection recovered note 14 as “Ibid.” from overlapping text on PDF p. 24. Its association retains the prior note’s reference boundary.

sections.heading: Focused claim audit follow-up
sections.body: The follow-up reviewed 10 individual claims from this report. The findings include 4 supported, 0 requiring correction, and 6 requiring further investigation. See the corresponding claim rows for PDF passages, evidence and unresolved questions. The numbered citation census above tracks the footnote records separately.

sections.heading: Additional claim audits
sections.body: The second follow-up reviewed 5 individual claims from this report. The findings include 4 supported, 0 requiring correction, and 1 requiring further investigation. See the corresponding claim rows for PDF passages, evidence and unresolved questions. The numbered citation census above tracks the footnote records separately.

sections.body: This pass recorded source decisions for 16 rows, including 0 with a complete recorded passage finding and 1 with a partial comparison. The report has 22 indexed numbered citation positions, including 0 newly recovered positions. The coverage panel records missing editions, unresolved shorthand and other source gaps.

Public edition or locator missing (1). Source identification or meaning unclear (1). Outside evidence review scope (3). The linked source rows retain each note's position and available evidence.
